description.ncbi_summary: This gene belongs to the glutathione peroxidase family. It is specifically expressed in the epididymis in the mammalian male reproductive tract, and is androgen-regulated. Unlike several other characterized glutathione peroxidases, this enzyme is not a selenoprotein, lacking the selenocysteine residue. Thus, it is selenium-independent, and has been proposed to play a role in protecting the membranes of spermatozoa from the damaging effects of lipid peroxidation and/or preventing premature acrosome reaction. Alternatively spliced transcript variants have been found for this gene. [provided by RefSeq, Oct 2016].

uniprot_function.text: Selenium-independent member of the glutathione peroxidase family that acts as a secreted antioxidant enzyme in the epididymal lumen, where it protects maturing spermatozoa from oxidative damage. Uses a catalytic cysteine rather than selenocysteine and displays peroxidase activity toward hydrogen peroxide and organic hydroperoxides, although classical selenocysteine-dependent glutathione peroxidase activity toward H2O2 is not detected in vitro and the physiological reducing substrate remains unclear (By similarity). Based on homologous cysteine-containing GPXs from plants, insects and protists, may preferentially use thioredoxin rather than glutathione as electron donor (By similarity). Required during epididymal transit to limit lipid peroxidation and oxidative DNA damage in spermatozoa, thereby preserving sperm DNA integrity and paternal genome quality (By similarity). Also localizes to the acrosomal region of epididymal spermatozoa and helps prevent premature acrosome reaction, possibly through a non-enzymatic mechanism involving sequestration of lipid peroxides from phospholipase A2, thereby contributing to sperm fertilizing ability (By similarity).
